title: CLO 2024.2 - Geometry Extrusion Direction
description: In 2024.2, the settings related to panel thickness are placed under the "Geometry" category in the Property Editor, making your garment creation process smoother!
transcript:
From version 2024.2 onward, all settings related to board thickness have been consolidated, including new functions.  
Overall operation will be smoother.  
In the property editor, a new set of categories has been added.  
The thickness rendering function has been moved here to allow increasing the board thickness by a relatively large rendering thickness.  
This ensures that the board thickness is visible only when it is located on the surface of the dense texture.  

**Squeeze Out Direction Option**  
You can set the direction of the board thickness.  
The default squeeze out direction is “all.”  
At this setting, the thickness will be displayed on both the front and back of the board.  
The squeeze out direction can be changed to “before” or “after.”  
You can make the board thickness exist only on the front or back of the board.  
Here, change back to “all.”  

You can choose whether to display or hide the front and back of the board.  
Open the default.  
Open the display.  
This is the grid.  
Hide the front.  
Hide the back.  

The sewing area can be controlled.  
The grid on the side of the board shows that the default is closed.  
The sides of the two boards have been sewn.  
The grid on the sewing area relates to the total thickness of the board.  

The total thickness of the board includes:  
- The thickness of the material itself.  
- The thickness of Vince (?).  
- The thickness on the board.  

You can select the corresponding fabric in the material window.  
Then, in the property editor, at the bottom, find the thickness.  
This material has a thickness of 0.5.  

**Thickness Selection Board**  
In the property editor, you can see the corresponding thickness, which is the thickness of the board.  
If the total thickness is equal, then the side mesh of the seam allowance will be hidden.  
The thickness of this panel is also set to 10.  
If you pull the panel a little bit, you can see that the side mesh of the seam allowance is hidden.  

At this time, you can open or close the display of the seam allowance.  
The mesh of the side seam allowance can be displayed or hidden.  
The panel on this side behaves the same way.  
This is the case when the total thickness is equal.  

If the total thickness is not equal,  
Select a panel.  
Increase the thickness of its seam allowance to 11.  
This panel is relatively thick, so its side mesh is not hidden.  
The side mesh of the relatively thin panel is hidden.  
Pull the panel a little bit.  
This is due to the different thicknesses of the seam allowance.  

When the panel is changed to the same seam allowance thickness,  
Apply another fabric to this panel.  
The thickness of this fabric is by default 0.5.  
Change it to 0.6.  
The effect that appears is the same as before.  
The side mesh of the relatively thick panel has been displayed.  

At this time, open or close the seam allowance display.  
The mesh is displayed.  
The relatively thin panel can freely display or hide the side mesh.  

As before,  
You can adjust the side mesh of the panel by adjusting the curve value.  
Turn off the display mesh first.  
Adjust the curve.  
The curve on the side of the panel changes over time.  
Open the display mesh again.  
Restore the curve.  

**Detail level controls the number of divisions of the side mesh.**  
Change to 2.  
The side now has only two layers of mesh.  
You can freely enter a number between 1 and 10 here.  
The double-layer performance of the panel is also controlled here.  

Next, I will show you the use of four applications.  
See the right pocket of the coat.  
This kind of single-line pocket.  
We want to create this effect, that is, the panel of the lip is slightly lower than the body panel.  
Then we can use the output direction function to achieve this effect.  

Select the lip panel of the left pocket to make it face out.  
Then select the output direction.  
After that, you can make the lip face in.  
The body panel is set to the output direction “front.”  
This is equivalent to raising the body.  
This is the effect from the side.  

Switch to 3D and 2D display.  
Select the seam line of the lip and the front piece.  
Change to reverse.  
Select seam line B.  
At this time, the effect is more obvious.  

See the inner top of the T-shirt.  
You can operate it similarly.  
The output direction of the lip panel is set to “back.”  
The front of the T-shirt is set to “front.”  
You can already see the effect from the side.  

Finally, select the seam line of the lip.  
You can change it to one,  
Or,  
You can move the part of the lip like this.  

At this time,  
The lip of the lapel in front of the shirt,  
You can try to align it along the side of the lip.  
Move the lip in the opposite direction.  

The model surface of the model in this file is 0.  
Select the shoulder strap. The conflict thickness of the shoulder strap plate is 2.  
Change it to 1 and then simulate.  
The gap becomes smaller.  
Return the conflict thickness to 2.  

In some cases, the conflict thickness cannot be changed.  
At this time, you can use the squeeze direction to optimize the performance of the shoulder strap.  
That is, change the squeeze direction of the shoulder strap plate to one side of the model body.  

If you are not sure about the front and back of the plate, switch to the black and white surface.  
White is front, gray is back.  
Switch back to the thick texture surface.  
The opposite side of the shoulder strap plate faces the model.  
Change the squeeze direction accordingly.  
The shoulder strap is close to the model.  

The zipper of the shoulder strap and the single-thread pocket in front use the same operation.  
No further explanation here.  

In addition, when making accessories, you can also use the squeeze direction  
To achieve specific effects.  

Now I want to create a concave effect on the shoulder strap.  
You should consider the different thicknesses of the shoulder strap plate.  
The shoulder strap plate is set to (value not specified).  
The shoulder strap plate is set to (value not specified).  
From the front, the effect is good.  
But when you turn to the back, you will find there is also a concave line on the back.  

If you want to keep the back flat,  
Only the front having a concave line,  
Change all the squeeze directions of the shoulder strap to (value not specified).  
At this time, the back is flat.  

Select the self-made shoulder strap.  
Also apply white fabric.  
There is no trace on the back.  
This is the front.  
The front shows this effect.  

I look forward to exploring more ways of use.

chunks.content: # CLO 2024.2 - Geometry Extrusion Direction This document explains the new features and settings related to board thickness and extrusion direction introduced in CLO version 2024.2. It covers the consolidation of thickness controls, squeeze out direction options, seam allowance behavior, side mesh details, and practical applications such as pocket lip extrusion and shoulder strap adjustments. These features optimize garment modeling by controlling visibility, thickness rendering, and fabric behavior in 3D simulation. --- ## Consolidated Board Thickness Settings and Rendering From CLO version 2024.2 onward, all board thickness settings have been unified under a new property editor category, improving workflow and functionality. - **Thickness Rendering Function:** Moved into the new property editor category to allow increasing board thickness through a relative rendering thickness parameter. - This enhancement ensures the board thickness is visible only on the surface of dense textures, improving visual clarity. - **Property Editor Categories:** A new set of categories has been added for easier management of thickness-related properties across different materials and parts. --- ## Squeeze Out Direction: Control of Board Thickness Orientation This section explains the squeeze out direction options, which control on which side(s) the board thickness is applied. - **Default Setting:** - The default squeeze out direction is **"all"**, meaning thickness is added on both the front and back surfaces of the board. - **Options:** - **Before:** Thickness exists only on the front side of the board. - **After:** Thickness exists only on the back side of the board. - These options allow for precise control of thickness visibility depending on garment requirements. - **Display Controls:** - You can independently display or hide the front and back of the board. - Visibility toggles include options to show/hide the front, back, or both surfaces, aiding detailed inspection during design. --- ## Sewing Area and Total Thickness Composition This section covers the behavior of the sewing area relative to board thickness and how total thickness is calculated. - **Sewing Area Control:** - The sewing grid on the side of the board indicates whether the seam is closed or open. - By default, the seam on the sides of joined boards is closed, meaning the mesh will show a continuous seam allowance. - **Total Thickness Includes:** 1. Material thickness (from fabric selection) 2. Thickness of Vince (a specific internal layer or component) 3. Thickness on the board itself (extrusion thickness) - **Material Thickness Selection:** - Choose fabrics in the material window, which have intrinsic thickness values (e.g., 0.5 mm). - These thickness values reflect in the property editor and affect the total thickness calculation. --- ## Thickness Selection Board and Seam Allowance Visibility This section details how seam allowance side meshes behave depending on thickness equality. - **Equal Total Thickness:** - When adjacent panels have the same total thickness, the seam allowance side mesh is hidden to create a seamless connection. - Example: A panel with thickness 10 and its adjacent panel also 10 will hide the side mesh when pulled apart slightly.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.2 - Geometry Extrusion Direction
chunks.content: - These thickness values reflect in the property editor and affect the total thickness calculation. --- ## Thickness Selection Board and Seam Allowance Visibility This section details how seam allowance side meshes behave depending on thickness equality. - **Equal Total Thickness:** - When adjacent panels have the same total thickness, the seam allowance side mesh is hidden to create a seamless connection. - Example: A panel with thickness 10 and its adjacent panel also 10 will hide the side mesh when pulled apart slightly. - **Unequal Total Thickness:** - If one panel's total thickness is increased (e.g., seam allowance thickness set to 11), the side mesh of the thicker panel remains visible. - The thinner panel’s side mesh is hidden, visually representing the difference in thickness. - **Fabric Changes Affect Thickness:** - Changing a panel’s fabric thickness (e.g., from 0.5 to 0.6) alters total thickness and mesh visibility similarly. - **Seam Allowance Display Toggle:** - You can open or close the display of seam allowance meshes independently, allowing better visualization of garment structure. --- ## Curve Adjustment and Detail Level of Side Mesh This section explains how to control the side mesh density and shape through curve adjustment and detail level settings. - **Curve Adjustment:** - By turning off the mesh display, you can adjust the curve controlling the side mesh shape over time. - After adjustment, re-enable the mesh display to see changes reflected. - **Detail Level Control:** - The detail level determines the number of divisions in the side mesh, adjustable between 1 and 10. - For example, setting detail level to 2 creates a side mesh with only two layers, affecting visual smoothness and performance. --- ## Practical Application: Pocket Lip Extrusion Direction This section demonstrates how to use the extrusion direction to create design effects, such as a pocket lip slightly lower than the body panel. - **Procedure:** 1. Select the lip panel of the pocket. 2. Set the output direction to face outward or inward as needed. 3. Set the body panel’s extrusion direction to "front" to raise or lower relative to the lip. - **Visualization:** - Switch between 3D and 2D views for detailed inspection. - Select seam lines and change their direction (e.g., reverse seam line B) to enhance effects. - **Example:** - For a T-shirt inner top, set the lip panel’s output direction to "back" and the front panel to "front" to create a layered effect. - **Seam Line Modification:** - Seam lines can be individually adjusted or moved to refine the lip position and effect. --- ## Shoulder Strap Thickness and Squeeze Direction Optimization This section covers how to manage thickness conflicts and optimize extrusion direction for shoulder straps. - **Conflict Thickness Adjustment:** - The default conflict thickness of shoulder strap plates is 2. - Reducing it to 1 decreases gaps in the simulation. - Some cases prevent changing conflict thickness directly; in these cases, adjust squeeze direction to one side of the model body instead.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.2 - Geometry Extrusion Direction
chunks.content: - **Seam Line Modification:** - Seam lines can be individually adjusted or moved to refine the lip position and effect. --- ## Shoulder Strap Thickness and Squeeze Direction Optimization This section covers how to manage thickness conflicts and optimize extrusion direction for shoulder straps. - **Conflict Thickness Adjustment:** - The default conflict thickness of shoulder strap plates is 2. - Reducing it to 1 decreases gaps in the simulation. - Some cases prevent changing conflict thickness directly; in these cases, adjust squeeze direction to one side of the model body instead. - **Front/Back Identification:** - Switch to the black-and-white surface mode to distinguish front (white) from back (gray). - Adjust squeeze direction so the strap faces the model correctly, ensuring proper proximity and fit. - **Same Operation for Similar Parts:** - The zipper on the shoulder strap and single-thread pockets use the same extrusion direction controls. --- ## Creating Concave Effects with Squeeze Direction This section explains how to create concave surface effects on parts like shoulder straps by controlling extrusion direction and thickness. - **Concave Effect Challenge:** - Applying thickness on both sides creates concave lines on front and back surfaces. - If a flat back surface is desired with concave front only, set all squeeze directions of the shoulder strap to one side. - **Fabric Application:** - Applying the same fabric on self-made shoulder straps shows no back trace, confirming correct extrusion direction. --- ## Summary CLO 2024.2 introduces refined control over board thickness and extrusion directions with consolidated settings in the property editor. These features enable precise visualization and simulation of garment components, including seam allowances, mesh detail, and directional thickness application. Practical applications such as pocket lip extrusion and shoulder strap optimization illustrate the enhanced capabilities for detailed garment modeling and fitting.
